newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW-CARNEGIE WANTS TOP 3 POSITION IN FINLAND.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CARNEGIE WANTS TOP 3 POSITION IN FINLAND.

text.p: Broker Carnegie Securities, which announced earlier it would buy local rival Erik Selin, aims to be among Finland's three biggest brokerage houses, managing director Matti Kinnunen said.

In an interview with Reuters, he said he expected competition to cut the biggest brokers' market shares to 12-13 percent and that a share of eight to 10 percent of the market -- which he said is normal for Carnegie -- should be enough.
"We aim to be on the medal stand in the markets wherever we operate," Kinnunen said.

Carnegie said it would buy Pankkiiriliike Erik Selin, including its fund management operations, for an undiclosed sum from Carolus Rosenlew, and said it would make its Finnish brokerage subsidiary a branch directly under the Swedish operation.

Finland's biggest broker Merita Pankkiiriliike, part of banking group Merita , has been losing market share and according to the latest bourse statistics, its market share of stock trading to end-May this year was 17.7 percent.
Alfred Berg - part of Dutch group ABN Amro -- was second with 12.3 percent, Evli third with 11.2 percent and Carnegie's and Selin's joint market share was 9.3 percent.
"I would consider above 10 percent in Finland very good, and below eight percent would be rather weak," Kinnunen said.
He expected Finland to be touched by the international trend of polarisation among brokerage houses, which leads them either to form bigger entities or find special niches.
"I think there will be more deals and investments like this," he said.

Carnegie -- controlled by UK investment bank Singer&Friedlander -- would focus on all its three business areas in Finland; broking and corporate finance which it had from before, and fund management which it got with Selin.
Kinnunen said Selin was a good match for Carnegie since it has a strong client base among Finnish institutional investors while Carnegie has an international client base.
"As it is at the moment, we complement each other very well ... and we will need all the people we have," he said.
Carnegie said in a statement it employs 30 people in Finland. The new group will employ a good 50 people. Selin has about 22 employees, Kinnunen said.

In connection with the merger, Carnegie's Finnish managing director Magnus von Knorring resigned and Kinnunen -- who runs the Swedish operation -- will take over for an interim period until a local head for the branch can be appointed.

Kinnunen expected the Finnish stock broking market to undergo a similar development as the Swedish market, where the number of brokerages has risen to 50 -- half internationally controlled -- from 27 -- almost all Swedish-owned -- since 1992.
